arxiv-2003-06000.title: Human Grasp Classification for Reactive Human-to-Robot Handovers
arxiv-2003-06000.creator: Wei Yang*, Chris Paxton*, Maya Cakmak, Dieter Fox
arxiv-2003-06000.description: Abstract Transfer of objects between humans and robots is a critical capability for collaborative robots. Although there has been a recent surge of interest in human-robot handovers, most prior research focus on robot-to-human handovers. Further, work on the equally critical human-to-robot handovers often assumes humans can place the object in the robot’s gripper.

arxiv-2012-11626.title: Partial order on passive states and Hoffman majorization in quantum thermodynamics
arxiv-2012-11626.creator: Uttam Singh, Siddhartha Das, Nicolas J. Cerf
arxiv-2012-11626.description: Abstract Passive states, i.e., those states from which no work can be extracted via unitary operations, play an important role in the foundations and applications of quantum thermodynamics. They generalize the familiar Gibbs thermal states, which are the sole passive states being stable under tensor product.

Fitzgerald,
arxiv-2302-04893.description: Abstract The HR 2562 system is a rare case where a brown dwarf companion resides in a cleared inner hole of a debris disk, offering invaluable opportunities to study the dynamical interaction between a substellar companion and a dusty disk.

arxiv-2309-14095.title: Velocity-resolved high- J J CO emission from massive star-forming clumps
arxiv-2309-14095.creator: Hoang Thanh Dat ,, Agata Karska, Min Young Lee, Friedrich Wyrowski, Le Ngoc Tram, Aiyuan Y. Yang, Karl M. Menten
arxiv-2309-14095.description: Abstract Context. Massive star formation is associated with energetic processes, which result in significant gas cooling via far-infrared (IR) lines. Velocity-resolved observations can constrain the kinematics of the gas, allowing the identification of the physical mechanisms responsible for gas heating. Aims.

arxiv-2510-24654.creator: Pengcheng Qiu, Chaoyi Wu, Junwei Liu, Qiaoyu Zheng, Yusheng Liao, Haowen Wang, Yun Yue, Qianrui Fan, Shuai Zhen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Ya Zhang, Weidi Xie

In this paper, we present a framework for training large language models (LLMs) as diagnostic agents with reinforcement learning, enabling them to manage multi - turn diagnostic processes, adaptively select examinations, and commit to final diagnoses.

arxiv-2511-19178.title: Chaotic dynamics for the two body problem on a sphere
arxiv-2511-19178.creator: Sergey Bolotin
arxiv-2511-19178.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sergey Bolotin. We prove the existence of chaotic trajectories for the two body problem on a sphere. The trajectories we construct encounter near-collisions and are similar to the second species solutions of Poincaré of the classical 3 body problem. The construction uses a general result on Lagrangian systems with Newtonian singularities of the potential which is based on the method of anti-integrable limit of Serge Aubry.

arxiv-2601-01113.title: Singly heavy Cascade Baryon Ξ c 0 \Xi^{0}_{c} & Ξ b − \Xi^{-}_{b} Spectroscopy in the Relativistic Framework of Independent Quark Model
arxiv-2601-01113.creator: Rameshri V. Patel, Manan Shah, Bhoomika Pandya
arxiv-2601-01113.description: Abstract In this work, the potential parameters of the independent quark model are systematically reduced using previously determined inputs from a broad range of baryons. The reduced-parameter formulation, developed within the relativistic Dirac formalism and employing a Martin-like potential, is then applied to the spectroscopy of the singly heavy baryons Ξ c 0 \Xi_{c}^{0} and Ξ b − \Xi_{b}^{-} .

arxiv-2602-21079.title: On thermal transpiration and thermomolecular pressure difference
arxiv-2602-21079.creator: I-Kun Chen, Kai-Li Wang
arxiv-2602-21079.description: Abstract In this article, we demonstrate the phenomenon of thermal transpiration in a bounded convex domain. We employ the stationary Boltzmann equation with a cutoff potential. For boundary condition, we partition the boundary into diffuse reflection and incoming regions. We establish the existence of solution in a weighted L ∞ L^{\infty} space.

pmc-11502733.title: Visualizing Research Trends in Quantum Dots for Health: A Bibliometric Exploration
pmc-11502733.creator: Remya Krishnan M, Sreya P, Shaija P.B, Saiju D.I, Jobin Jose
pmc-11502733.description: Quantum dots (QDs) are semiconductor nanoparticles with immense potential accompanied by unique optoelectronic properties for revolutionizing several biomedical applications related to imaging, diagnostics, drug delivery, and therapy. A detailed bibliometric analysis has been performed in this article with regard to research relating to QDs in the health sector during 2004-2024.

pmc-11689203.title: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF THE PATIENT-DRIVEN PAYMENT MODEL ON NURSING HOME CARE QUALITY: A STAFFING PERSPECTIVE
pmc-11689203.creator: Gregory Orewa, Robert Weech-Maldonado, Ganisher Davlyatov, Justin Lord, David Becker, Sue Feldman
pmc-11689203.description: The Patient-Driven Payment Model (PDPM) launched on October 1, 2019, restructured Medicare payments to reflect resident needs over service quantity, aiming to improve quality and efficiency in nursing homes (NH). PDPM’s shift towards resident needs (rather than therapy minutes) may lead to greater nurse utilization, which may potentially improve the quality of care.

pmc-11716558.title: Age‐related differences in the relationship between sleep quality and cortical thickness
pmc-11716558.creator: Hyun Kim, Yisha Zhang, Benjamin Huber, Elizabeth Rueppel, Terry E Goldberg, Seonjoo Lee, human connectome project
pmc-11716558.description: BackgroundWhile the association between sleep quality and brain health is well established, the role of aging in this relationship is largely unknown. This study aimed to examine the interaction between sleep and age on cortical thickness using samples from large‐scale cohort studies.

pmc-12404638.title: Deep neural networks explain spiking activity in auditory cortex
pmc-12404638.creator: Bilal Ahmed, Joshua D. Downer, Brian J. Malone, Joseph G. Makin, Hugues Berry, Jian Liu, Hugues Berry, Jian Liu, Hugues Berry, Jian Liu, Hugues Berry, Jian Liu
pmc-12404638.description: For static stimuli or at gross (∼1-s) time scales, artificial neural networks (ANNs) that have been trained on challenging engineering tasks, like image classification and automatic speech recognition, are now the best predictors of neural responses in primate visual and auditory cortex.

pmc-12875977.title: Effect of bedside comprehensive ability training on teaching and training in operating room
pmc-12875977.creator: Yi Zhong, Wenjun Bu, Qifan Li, Lili Zheng
pmc-12875977.description: AimTo assess the effect of bedside comprehensive ability training on teaching and training in operating room.MethodsOne hundred and thirty female clinical nurses who joined our hospital from January 2019 to December 2021 were randomly assigned to a control group and an observation group. The control group adopted problem-based learning (PBL), while the observation group adopted bedside comprehensive ability training.

pmc-13205623.title: Synergistic Mechanisms of Surfactants and Monovalent Ions for Enhanced Oil Recovery Through Interfacial Properties and Microfluidic Study
pmc-13205623.creator: Xuchun Yang, Yafei Liu, Fen He, Chenlu Du, Jingdi Zheng, Desheng Zhou
pmc-13205623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In oil and gas development, the oil displacement efficiency of single surfactants is inherently constrained. While synergistic interactions between salt ions and surfactants can enhance displacement performance by modulating interfacial properties and wettability, the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. This study systematically investigated the synergistic effects of two monovalent salts (NaCl, KCl) and four surfactants through macroscopic characterization of interfacial property and microfluidic displacement experiments using microfluidic device with dead-end structures.

pmc-13630638.creator: Yi Cui, Qiannan Zhao, Jianning Zhang, Siyu Lu, Shuai Li, Lufeng Zhao, Ming Gao, Hao Chen, Hui Han, Xiaofang Huang
pmc-13630638.description: BackgroundEvidence for nebulized colistimethate sodium (CMS) in hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) remains inconsistent, potentially due to heterogeneity in airway conditions and delivery timing. We evaluated whether timely initiation of nebulized CMS following bronchodilator airway pre-treatment was associated with microbiological outcomes in critically ill patients.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3673.title: 18 U.S.C. § 3673 — Definitions for sentencing provisions
uslaw-usc-t18-s3673.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s3673.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 232 (Miscellaneous Sentencing Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. As used in chapters 227 and 229— (1) the term “found guilty” includes acceptance by a court of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere; (2) the term “commission of an offense” includes the attempted commission of an offense.
